subject: basic-computing
title: Securing the Computer System
meta: Lesson practice set · Question types of the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: Practice set for this lesson in the question types of the April 2026 paper.
Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

questions.q: What is the role of an Antivirus software?
questions.answer: It protects the system from viruses, worms, Trojans and other malware.

questions.q: What is the function of Antivirus Program?
questions.answer: To detect, block and remove viruses and other malware from the computer.

questions.q: Define cyber crime and give examples.
questions.answer: Cyber crime is any unlawful act done using digital devices connected to the internet; examples are online fraud, identity theft, cyber bullying and copyright infringement.

questions.q: Define 'Recycling' with reference to E-waste management.
questions.answer: Recycling is converting e-waste into something that can be used again, by dismantling devices and extracting metals like copper and gold.

questions.q: What is the full form of WEEE?
questions.answer: Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment.

questions.q: Which are the most feasible methods of E-waste management?
questions.answer: Recycling, refurbishing and re-use.

questions.q: Define E-waste management.
questions.answer: The efficient disposal of e-waste in a way that is less harmful to people and the environment.

questions.q: List two harmful effects of E-waste.
questions.answer: Lead causes brain and kidney damage; mercury causes respiratory disorders and brain damage; it pollutes air, water and soil (any two).

questions.q: What precautions are to be taken for password protection of a system? Mention two points.
questions.answer: Do not share passwords and do not use the same password for all applications; make it strong with letters, digits and special characters.

questions.q: Which chemical is created when a motherboard is burnt?
questions.answer: Beryllium.

questions.q: What acts as a barrier between a computer and the internet?
questions.answer: A firewall.

questions.q: What is spyware?
questions.answer: A malware designed to secretly gather information from a system and send it to a third party.

questions.q: Which Act is the primary cyber law in India?
questions.answer: The IT Act 2000.

questions.q: Name the process in which electronics are sold again at lower prices.
questions.answer: Refurbishing.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: What is an Antivirus software? What precaution must one take while using any antivirus program?
questions.answer: Antivirus software protects the system from viruses and malware. Precautions: install only original antivirus, update it regularly, and remember it gives no 100% assurance so also scan files and avoid unknown links.

questions.q: How do mercury and plastic material found in E-waste harm the human body?
questions.answer: Mercury causes respiratory disorders and brain damage; plastics react with air and moisture, damage the immune system and cause stress and anxiety.

questions.q: Define cyber security.
questions.answer: The processes, practices and techniques to protect devices, networks, data and programs from attack, damage or unauthorized access.

questions.q: Why is cyber security important? Give three points.
questions.answer: Data is available to everyone and needs protection; organizational data must not be leaked; personal information on social media can be hacked; national security needs protection from digital spying (any three).

questions.q: What points should be kept in mind while setting passwords?
questions.answer: Do not share it, use different passwords for different applications, use letters, digits and special characters, avoid initials and date of birth, keep it 8–10 characters.

questions.q: Name any four salient features of the IT Act 2000.
questions.answer: Legal recognition of electronic transactions; legal recognition of digital signatures; online correspondence with government; legal electronic storage of data; penalties for cyber crime (any four).

questions.q: Write any two advantages of Cyber Law.
questions.answer: It addresses security of data and services; it encourages healthy trade; digital signatures make exchange of documents easy; it improves e-governance (any two).

questions.q: Why should e-waste not be dumped in a landfill?
questions.answer: Toxic chemicals leach out and contaminate groundwater and soil, which may reach drinking water.

questions.q: Differentiate between recycling and refurbishing.
questions.answer: Recycling converts e-waste into reusable material by extracting metals; refurbishing renovates the device and sells it again at a lower price.

questions.q: What is a firewall? How is it enabled?
questions.answer: A firewall (hardware or software) acts as a barrier between the computer or network and the internet; it can be enabled through Control Panel, System and Security.

questions.q: How can a cyber crime be reported?
questions.answer: To the cyber cell of the local police station or online at the cyber crime portal, where complaints can be anonymous.

questions.q: Why should we back up our data and uninstall unused programs?
questions.answer: A backup on secondary storage or cloud saves data if the system is hacked or the disk crashes; uninstalling unused programs keeps the system secure and faster.

sections.title: Answer the questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain the steps to be taken to secure your system (any six).
questions.answer: Password protect the system; update OS and software; heed security warnings; install original antivirus; do not open unsolicited mails; download from official sites; scan files; enable the firewall; adjust browser settings; use anti-spyware; back up data.

questions.q: Explain the acts that come under cyber crime.
questions.answer: Online fraud such as credit card theft, copyright infringement, defamation, cyber stalking and bullying, violation of business trade secrets and identity theft.

questions.q: Explain the salient features of the IT Act 2000.
questions.answer: It gives legal recognition to electronic transactions and digital signatures, allows online dealings with government and online money transfer, permits electronic records, and lists offences, penalties and trial procedure including cyber terrorism.

questions.q: Explain the harmful effects of e-waste.
questions.answer: Lead damages the brain, nervous system and kidneys; mercury causes respiratory problems and brain damage; plastics harm the immune system and cause stress; burning produces beryllium that causes lung cancer, skin diseases and allergies.

questions.q: Explain the methods of e-waste management.
questions.answer: Recycling converts e-waste to reusable material; refurbishing renovates devices and sells them cheaply; re-use means using the device again after slight modification. The government should set up recycling units and enforce laws.

questions.q: Explain the need for cyber security.
questions.answer: Data is accessible to all so must be protected; organizations share confidential data; personal data on social sites can be hacked; cyber attacks threaten national security.

questions.q: What is a firewall and what are spyware and its protection?
questions.answer: A firewall blocks communication between a device and the internet to protect from threats; spyware secretly collects bank and card details; anti-spy software, often built into antivirus, protects against spyware, adware and Trojans.
